# Wire fixtures

Golden files for every tenant-facing surface the provider implements, so a tenant implementation (rig's TypeScript client, or any other) can test against the exact bytes the provider accepts and emits without the provider running. Filed as toon-protocol/TOON_Network#16, extended with the Milestone 2 wire shapes by #19.

**Where they come from.** Every file under [`wire/`](wire/) is generated by the provider's wire tests — `tests/wire_fixtures.rs` in the `toon-provider` crate — from the real HTTP surface and the real event builders, over fixed test keys, a fixed clock and reproducible signatures. Nothing in a fixture is typed by hand. The provider's `cargo test` (and so its CI) verifies the files byte-for-byte against the code and fails on drift, so a wire change that is not reflected here fails the provider's build. This directory is a copy; the provider's `tests/fixtures/wire/` is the source.

**Kind numbers** are the provider's `src/nostr/kinds.rs` constants at generation time (`constants.json` → `kinds`). If a number moves, the fixtures are regenerated and the copy re-synced; a tenant should read kinds from `constants.json`, not hard-code them.

## Commands

| Task | Where | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Verify the fixtures against the provider code (what CI does) | provider repo | `cargo test --test wire_fixtures` (or `make fixtures-check`) |
| Regenerate after an intended wire change | provider repo | `make fixtures` (runs `TOON_UPDATE_FIXTURES=1 cargo test --test wire_fixtures`; stale files are removed first) |
| Regenerate **and** sync this copy | provider repo | `make fixtures TOON_SPEC_DIR=<path to this repository>` |
| Sync this copy only | provider repo | `make fixtures-sync TOON_SPEC_DIR=<path to this repository>` |
| Check this copy the way a tenant would (no dependencies) | this repo | `node docs/spec/fixtures/check.mjs` |

`check.mjs` recomputes every event's NIP-01 id, verifies every BIP-340 signature with a standard-library-only implementation, checks that every signed body is exactly `{ "request": <event> }`, and derives the `<addr>.<listing>.v<n>.spawn` routes from the Listing events to compare with `routes.listing.json`. For the §8 events it also checks that each is signed by the publisher rather than the provider, that an entry's and a record's `d` and `x` tags agree with the digest in content, that a Blob Record's parts sum to its size with only the last one short, and that a Template carries no capability; for the spawn image forms, that `reference` and `registry_entry` are never both present.

## The fixed world

`constants.json` states it. In short:

- **Clock:** every event has `created_at = 1700000000`; the provider's clock is stopped there. Lease Requests expire 60 s later; leases last 3600 s.
- **Keys:** TEST-ONLY secret keys, published on purpose — tenant `11…11`, provider `22…22`, a second tenant `33…33`, publisher `44…44` (64 hex digits each). Never fund, trust or reuse them. The **publisher** signs the §8 events; a provider never does, which is why it needs a key of its own here.
- **Provider:** `ilp_address = g.fixture`, host `203.0.113.7`, one relay, one Solana USDC settlement leg, `isolation = shared-kernel`, two listings: `basic` v1 (capacity 2, capability `x-fixture`) and `gpu` v1 (capacity 1, `resources.gpu = rtx-4090`).
- **Signatures:** `id` is the SHA-256 of the NIP-01 serialization `[0, pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content]`; `sig` is BIP-340 Schnorr over `id`. Fixture signatures use **all-zero auxiliary randomness** (`aux_rand = 0x00 × 32`) so they are reproducible: `schnorr.sign(id, secret_key, zeros)` in any BIP-340 library gives the same 64 bytes. Real signers use fresh randomness; a verifier cannot tell the difference. For the directory events the provider signs with fresh randomness at runtime, so the fixture re-signs the identical event (same id, tags, content) with zero aux — every byte except `sig` is what the provider produced, and the id is re-verified in the test.
- **JSON:** pretty-printed, object keys sorted, trailing newline. Key order is insignificant everywhere; the NIP-01 id is computed over the array form, which each event fixture includes verbatim as `nip01_serialization`.

## Files

Each file is named `<surface>.<case>.json` and carries a `fixture` header (`surface`, `case`, `description`, `generated_by`).

**Constants and keys**

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `constants.json` | Clock, TTLs, test keys (tenant, provider, other tenant, publisher), kind numbers, label, signing rule |

**Lease Requests** (`event`, parsed `content`, `nip01_serialization`, and `packet_body` — the exact request body)

| File | Op | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `lease_request.spawn.json` | `spawn` | Full spawn content (§6.2): `workload_id`, `image`, `env`, `ports`, `volume_gb`, `ssh_public_key`, `entrypoint`, `args` |
| `lease_request.status.json` | `status` | `{ "workload_id" }` |
| `lease_request.terminate.json` | `terminate` | `{ "workload_id" }` |

**Requests and responses** (`route`, `http_path`, `request_body`, `response_status`, `response_body`)

| File | Route | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| `availability.would_run.json` | `<addr>.availability` | Free, unsigned, `{ "would_run": true }` |
| `availability.refused.json` | `<addr>.availability` | HTTP 200 with `would_run: false`, `error`, `message` (a version not on sale) |
| `availability.image_unresolved.json` | `<addr>.availability` | The `refused_image` a tenant should meet here rather than buy on `.spawn`: an image named by digest alone |
| `spawn.ok.json` | `<addr>.basic.v1.spawn` | Body is `lease_request.spawn`'s packet body; answer has `role`, `expires_at = now + 3600`, `access` |
| `extend.ok.json` | `<addr>.basic.v1.extend` | Unsigned `{ "workload_id" }`; `expires_at` grows by one interval |
| `status.running.json` | `<addr>.status` | `state: "running"`, `access` present |
| `status.ended.json` | `<addr>.status` | After termination: `state: { "ended": "termination" }`, no `access` |
| `terminate.ok.json` | `<addr>.terminate` | `{ "workload_id", "state": { "ended": "termination" } }` |

**The three forms of a spawn's `image`** (spec §6.2). Each carries `image` (the object on its own), `spawn_content` (the whole parsed content), and the request and response of one spawn on `<addr>.basic.v1.spawn`.

| File | Form | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `spawn_image.reference.json` | `{ reference, digest }` | 200: pulled as `reference@digest` from an upstream registry. Also carries the informational `template`, which the provider parses and never reads (ADR 0004) |
| `spawn_image.registry_entry.json` | `{ digest, registry_entry: { address, relay } }` | 422 `refused_image`: this provider does not resolve the Image Registry (§8.4) yet |
| `spawn_image.digest_only.json` | `{ digest }` | 422 `refused_image`: the same message, and refused before capacity is counted or any container is created |

A fourth shape — `reference` together with `registry_entry`, a `digest` that is not `sha256:` plus 64 lowercase hex, a `registry_entry.address` that does not name kind `30434` — is `invalid_request`; `error.invalid_request.json` is the fixture for that class of refusal.

**Publisher events** (§8; `event`, parsed `content`, `nip01_serialization`). Signed by the **publisher** key, not the provider's, and each carrying `["L", "toon.network"]`.

| File | Kind | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| `registry.image_entry.json` | `K_IMAGE` | `d = "web:1.0"`, `x` = the image digest's hex, and `blobs` with BOTH source types: one `oci` (still upstream) and one `toon-store` (naming the Blob Record's own upload) |
| `registry.blob_record.json` | `K_BLOB` | `d` and `x` both name the blob; three ordered `parts`, two of `part_size` and a short last one, summing to `size` |
| `registry.template.json` | `K_TEMPLATE` | `d` = the template name; `image` by content address plus its registry entry, `ports`, `data_path`, `env_fixed`, `env_tenant`, `min_resources`. No capability field |

**Errors**, one per §5 code, in the spec's validation order (each carries `validation_step`). Statuses are this provider's HTTP mapping; the spec fixes only the JSON body.

| # | File | Status | How it was produced | Step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `error.bad_signature.json` | 403 | `lease_request.spawn` with one hex digit of `sig` changed | §6.2 step 1 |
| 2 | `error.stale_request.json` | 400 | Correctly signed, `expiration` in the past (also the code for a >300 s window and a replayed id) | §6.2 step 1 |
| 3 | `error.invalid_request.json` | 400 | Spawn content with an unknown field `privileged` (ADR 0004: refused, never dropped) | §6.2 step 1 |
| 4 | `error.wrong_listing_version.json` | 404 | Valid spawn paid on `basic.v2`, which is not sold | §6.2 step 2 |
| 5 | `error.workload_id_taken.json` | 409 | Second spawn naming a live lease's `workload_id` | §6.2 step 4 |
| 6 | `error.refused_image.json` | 422 | Provider's image policy denies the digest | §6.2 step 5 |
| 7 | `error.no_matching_arch.json` | 422 | OCI index with an arm64 manifest only, listing is amd64 | §6.2 step 5 |
| 8 | `error.no_capacity.json` | 409 | Third spawn on a capacity-2 listing | §6.2 step 6 |
| 9 | `error.unknown_workload.json` | 404 | Status for a `workload_id` this provider never leased | §6.3/§6.5/§6.6 |
| 10 | `error.not_tenant.json` | 403 | Status signed by the other tenant | §6.5 |
| 11 | `error.expired.json` | 409 | Extension of a terminated lease (`expired` covers every ending, §6.3) | §6.3 |
| 12 | `error.not_standby.json` | 409 | **Shape only** — see Milestone 3 below | §6.3 |

**Directory events** (`event`, parsed `content`, `nip01_serialization`)

| File | Kind | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| `directory.profile.json` | `K_PROFILE` | Every §4.1 field; `connector_seal_key` is what a tenant seals to (ADR 0011) |
| `directory.listing.json` | `K_LISTING` | `basic`: `d`, `a` → Profile coordinate `10432:<pubkey>:`, `L`, `l isolation:`, `l arch:`, one `t` per capability, `g` |
| `directory.listing.gpu.json` | `K_LISTING` | `gpu`: as above plus `resources.gpu` and `l gpu:<model>`, no `t` |
| `directory.liveness.json` | `K_LIVENESS` | `available` per listing at full capacity; `expiration = now + 5 × liveness_cadence_s` |
| `directory.eviction.json` | `K_EVICTION` | `x` tag = workload id; content `{ workload_id, reason, message }` |

**Routes**

| File | Shows |
|---|---|
| `routes.listing.json` | The connector route table the Profile and Listings generate: `prefix` (what a tenant pays), `price`, and the provider-internal `handler_url`. `check.mjs` derives `<addr>.<d>.v<version>.spawn` from each Listing event and confirms it is in the table. |

## Milestone 3 placeholders (not fixtures)

Warm Standby is not implemented in Milestone 1, so there are no fixtures for `<addr>.<listing>.v<n>.standby`, `<addr>.<listing>.v<n>.standby.extend`, a spawn with `standby_set`, a `role: "standby"` response without `access`, or a `K_TAKEOVER` event. Today a spawn carrying `standby_set` is refused `invalid_request` ("Standby Sets are not sold in this milestone"). `error.not_standby.json` is the one exception: it is the error shape as the provider's own serialiser and status mapping render it, with `route`, `http_path` and `request_body` set to `null` because no Milestone 1 route can produce it. When Milestone 3 lands, `tests/wire_fixtures.rs` grows the cases and this section goes.

## Where the fixtures follow the provider rather than the spec draft

The fixtures are what the Milestone 1 provider does. Where the spec draft and the provider disagree, the fixtures side with the code and the disagreement is listed here so it is resolved on purpose, not by accident:

- **Availability body.** `{ "listing", "version", "image": { … } }`, not §6.4's `image_digest` and `role`. The `image` is the same three-form object a spawn carries.
- **The Image Registry forms are `refused_image`, not resolved.** The provider parses all three forms of §6.2's `image`, and answers both Image Registry forms with `refused_image` and a message saying it does not yet resolve §8.4. That is the fixtures' state of the world, not a permanent rule; when the fetcher lands, `spawn_image.registry_entry` and `spawn_image.digest_only` become successful spawns and these files change. §8.4 now states the interim answer so a tenant can rely on it.
- **`min_resources` and `ports` in a Template.** §8.3 wrote both as `{…}`; the fixtures use the shapes the rest of the protocol already has — a Listing's `resources` (§4.2) and a spawn's `ports` (§6.2). §8.3 has been corrected to say so.
- **The `x` tag carries bare hex.** §8.1 and §8.2 wrote `"<digest hex>"` and `"<hex>"`; the provider writes the digest WITHOUT its `sha256:` prefix in both, while `d` keeps the prefix. §8.1 and §8.2 have been corrected to say so, as has the rule that a Blob Record part's `sha256` is bare hex too.
- **The §8 events carry `["L", "toon.network"]`.** §8 did not say so; the builders add it, and §8 has been corrected. They are signed by a publisher, never by a provider, which is why `constants.json` carries a fourth test key.
- **An entry address has four colon-separated fields.** §6.2 writes `30434:<pubkey>:<d>`, and an entry's `d` is itself `<name>:<tag>`, so the coordinate reads `30434:<pubkey>:<name>:<tag>` and must be split into at most three parts. §6.2 has been corrected to say so.
- **`state` on the wire.** §6.7 draws the states; the provider serialises them as `"provisioning" | "running" | { "ended": "expiry" | "termination" | "eviction" }`.
- **Termination answer.** §6.6 names none; the provider answers `{ "workload_id", "state" }`.
- **Eviction reasons.** §6.7 says "a reason code"; the provider's vocabulary is `abuse | policy | maintenance | other`, and its Eviction Notice also carries `["L", "toon.network"]`.
- **HTTP statuses.** The spec fixes only the JSON error body; the 400/403/404/409/422 mapping is this provider's (`provider_http::refuse`).
